script: In October 1959, voters in São Paulo, Brazil were so fed up with corruption and food shortages that thousands cast their vote for someone who wasn't even human. A local journalist, fed up with the candidates on offer, proposed a write-in joke: Cacareco, a five-year-old rhinoceros at the city zoo. It was supposed to be a punchline. Instead, she won. One hundred thousand votes - fifteen percent of the entire city, more than any other candidate. Five hundred and forty people ran for forty-five council seats that year. A rhinoceros beat every single one of them. Election officials had no legal way to seat an actual rhino, so they nullified every one of her votes and reran that race the following week. Her name outlived the scandal. Voto Cacareco - the Cacareco vote - is still Brazilian slang for a protest vote, more than sixty years later. Follow for more history too strange to make up.

metadata.title: Random But True: The Rhino Who Won An Election
metadata.caption:
In October 1959, voters in São Paulo, Brazil were so fed up with corruption and food shortages that thousands cast their vote for someone who wasn't even human.

A local journalist, unimpressed with the candidates on offer, proposed a write-in joke: Cacareco, a five-year-old rhinoceros living at the city zoo.

It was supposed to be a punchline. Instead, she won - one hundred thousand votes, about fifteen percent of the entire city, more than any of the other 540 candidates running for 45 council seats.

Election officials had no legal way to seat an actual rhino, so every one of her votes was nullified and the race was rerun the following week.

Her name outlived the scandal: "voto Cacareco" - the Cacareco vote - is still Brazilian slang for a protest vote, more than sixty years later.
